## Overview

Backpressure in a streaming pipeline is the mechanism by which a slow downstream consumer signals an upstream producer to reduce its emission rate, rather than letting an unbounded buffer grow until the process runs out of memory.

## Implementation Patterns

### Bounded Queues

Blocked producers: once a bounded queue reaches capacity, the producer cannot enqueue additional items and blocks until the consumer drains sufficient elements to make space available. This is a direct, synchronous blocking model.

### Credit-Based Flow Control

The consumer explicitly grants the producer permission to send N more items. The producer tracks available credits and stops emitting once credits are exhausted, waiting for the consumer to replenish them. This model enables asynchronous communication with predictable producer throttling.

### Reactive-Pull Models

The consumer requests items on its own schedule rather than the producer pushing them. This inverts the direction of control: the producer only emits when the consumer explicitly pulls, giving the consumer full governance over consumption rate.

## Value

Without backpressure, a fast producer can fill unbounded buffers until memory is exhausted, causing the entire pipeline to crash or degrade catastrophically. Backpressure allows pipelines to self-regulate by coupling producer and consumer rates.
